comparison: Perfect agreement on IP4 inhibition of P-Rex1 (C5, C21, C22, C23). Both evaluations find the evidence supported through in vitro GEF activity assays and specificity testing. Reviewers explicitly affirm the structural and biochemical evidence.

Perfect agreement on allosteric inhibition mechanism (C6, C25, C26). Both evaluations accept HDX-MS data showing IP4-induced protection and functional data demonstrating allosteric effects. Reviewers note high quality experimental data and thorough execution.

Agreement on cryo-EM structure and IP4 binding (C7, C27, C33, C34, C35). Both find evidence supported, though peer reviewers note novelty is compromised by Chang et al. 2022 structure being virtually identical, while still acknowledging the IP4 stabilization finding as significant.

Partial overlap on DH-DEP1 interface (C8, C48). OpenEval R4 focuses specifically on these claims, while peer R4 covers broader structural observations including PH-4HB interface (C9, C37, C39, C42, C43, C44). Both evaluations support the structural findings.

Partial overlap on PH-4HB interface. OpenEval R5 addresses C9, C37, C39, C42, C43, C44, C45 with cryo-EM and HDX-MS support. Peer R4 covers some of these claims (C9, C37, C39, C42, C43, C44) plus DH-DEP1 interface (C8, C48). Both find evidence supported.

Strong overlap on mutagenesis validation (C10, C57, C58, C59, C62). Both evaluations support the GEF activity assays showing interface disruption increases activity. Peer review also includes broader biophysical characterization claims.

Partial overlap on SAXS data. OpenEval R7 focuses on L177E variant conformational changes (C11, C68, C70). Peer R6 addresses biophysical characterization more broadly (C65, C66, C68, C69), accepting correlation between activity, stability, and conformation.

Partial overlap on interface mutants. OpenEval R8 covers C12, C63, C64, C66 with GEF assays and ThermoFluor analysis. Peer R5 addresses mutagenesis validation including C12, C63. Both find evidence supported.

Minimal overlap on activity-stability correlation. OpenEval R9 focuses on inverse correlation between activity and Tm (C65). Peer R6 accepts this as part of broader biophysical characterization supporting the structural model.

Strong agreement on cellular validation (C13, C77-C82, C84). Both evaluations support SRE luciferase and migration assays showing increased activity for interface-disrupting mutants. Peer review confirms both in vitro and cell-based assays are confirmatory.

Perfect agreement on PIP3-induced activation (C15, C16, C91-C97). Both evaluations accept HDX-MS data showing deprotection at autoinhibitory interfaces and increased dynamics with PIP3-containing liposomes. Reviewers note thorough execution and high quality data.

Strong agreement on DEP domain membrane binding (C86, C87, C89, C90). Both evaluations accept HDX-MS data showing protection of DEP domain loops. OpenEval also includes C88 on direct lipid interaction. Reviewers find experiments technically sound.

Agreement on physiological relevance of IP4 inhibition (C98, C99, C103). Both find IC50 within physiological range supported. However, peer reviewer notes 'the relevance of this in a cellular setting is not clear and is not experimentally demonstrated,' indicating some uncertainty about in vivo significance.

Overlap on physiological IP4 concentrations (C17, C103). OpenEval finds IC50 data supports physiological relevance. Peer review affirms significance but notes cellular relevance not experimentally demonstrated, showing partial agreement with some reservation.

Perfect agreement on structural comparison to unliganded P-Rex1 (C51-C55). Both evaluations accept that IP4-bound and unliganded structures are virtually identical, with IP4 acting by stiffening rather than reorganizing interfaces.

Disagreement on disulfide bond experiments (C71-C76). OpenEval finds evidence supported with appropriate caution. Peer reviewer specifically critiques these experiments as causing 'confusion for interpretation' and suggests moving to supplement, indicating uncertainty about clarity.

Agreement on fragment studies (C24). Both evaluations accept that IP4 has no effect on DH/PH or DH/PH-DEP1 fragments, supporting the allosteric mechanism. OpenEval also links to C128 on full-length requirement.

Agreement on 4HB domain identification (C30, C31). Both evaluations accept structural characterization and comparison to FAT domains. OpenEval covers additional structural details (C28, C29, C36) not specifically addressed in peer review.

Minimal overlap on SAXS characterization of specific mutants. OpenEval R25 addresses A170K and I409A Rg values (C69). Peer R6 accepts broader biophysical characterization including this data as supporting the model.

Minimal overlap on EGF control experiments. OpenEval R26 addresses specificity control showing no EGF effect (C83). Peer R7 accepts cellular validation broadly including this specificity, though C83 not explicitly mentioned.

Agreement on comprehensive activation model (C125-C130 overlap). Both evaluations accept the mechanistic model of PIP3/membrane/Gβγ-induced activation. Peer review notes similarity to Chang et al. 2022 model. OpenEval covers more extensive claim set (C115-C130).
